title: Unauthenticated bootstrap endpoints: prove host access with a one-time host-issued code
summary: When a surface must be usable before any sign-in exists (first-run setup), gate the unauthenticated endpoint on a one-time code issued on the host CLI rather than on loopback, Host or X-Forwarded-For, which Next.js surfaces cannot prove.
reusable_steps: When a surface must be usable before any sign-in exists (first-run setup), gate the unauthenticated endpoint on a one-time code issued on the host CLI rather than on loopback, Host or X-Forwarded-For, which Next
expected_outcome:
Applies to any Kyberion surface endpoint that must work before authentication exists (first-run owner claim, initial SSO configuration).

Rules:
1. Proof of server access = a code issued by a host CLI (`pnpm organization first-run code`). Store only a salted SHA-256 hash, an expiry (default 30 min) and a failed-attempt counter in a secret-guard document; compare with timingSafeEqual; lock after N failures; consume the code before any write so one code never authorizes two claims.
2. Put the code in the URL fragment (`#code=`) so it never reaches server or proxy logs; the page clears it with history.replaceState.
3. Validate input before spending an attempt, but disclose registry state (tenant/member suspended) only after a valid code, without consuming it.
4. Decide "still open" fail-closed: an explicit claimed marker OR any active owner that can already sign in (registry token or bound IdP identity), scanned with the strict member listing (`listMemberIdsStrict`) so an unreadable registry never reopens the bootstrap.
5. Instance-wide settings saved from the surface (OIDC) go to secret-guard with `backup: false` so a rotated/cleared secret does not linger in a .bak; responses expose only `client_secret_set`. Environment variables keep precedence as a whole set, so env-configured deployments are unaffected.
6. Accept and document residual risks instead of over-engineering: unauthenticated lockout is DoS only (host reissues the code); Next.js rate-limit keys collapse to a shared bucket without KYBERION_TRUST_PROXY.
